niche: a UK commercial bank's credit risk monitoring team forecasting how many obligor groups will move onto the watch list over the next twelve months, to size the 2027 watch-list caseload by exposure band, from an early-warning system whose entity signals reach a group from any member, borrowing or not, through the GLEIF consolidation hierarchy, and four closed annual cohorts of watch-list outcomes
answer: Put a 2027 caseload of 78 groups to the committee: 78 of the 913 obligor groups in the monitored book at 30 September 2026 are expected to reach the watch list by 30 September 2027.
stakeholder_role: head of credit risk monitoring at a UK commercial bank, who sizes the watch-list and workout caseload for the executive risk committee's 2027 resourcing budget

spine.entity: one legal entity's early-warning signal (colour, score and trigger codes) at one month-end, as the early-warning engine published it, keyed by LEI

world.org_type: UK commercial bank, credit risk monitoring

driver: An aggregate unit is flagged when any of its components signals, and a signal raised on a component that carries the unit's own obligations converts to the outcome at several times the rate of one raised only on a component reached through the ownership links; the forward pool's flags sit far more on obligation-carrying components than any closed cohort's did, so a single flagged rate carried from the cohorts undercounts the inflow, and only the conversion of each kind of flag, rebuilt by tracing every flag back to the component that raised it, carries forward.
driver_concrete: CRM-07 3.2 flags a group when any member is AMBER or RED: a customer the bank lends to, or a parent, sister or holding company reached only through the GLEIF consolidation records. Over the four closed cohorts a flag raised on a customer reached the watch list within the year 120 times in 240 and a flag raised only on a member the bank does not lend to 11 times in 176; this September's 165 flags are 77 per cent customer-raised against 48 to 69 per cent in the cohorts, so the cohorts' single flagged rate gives 64 and the conversion of each kind of flag gives 78.
stump: A competent solver rolls the entity signals up to groups, builds the four closed cohorts and gives each flagged group the share of flagged groups that reached the list over those cohorts taken together and each other group the unflagged share, and files 64; the step that lands it there is treating every group flag as one kind of signal, when a flag raised on a customer the bank lends to reaches the list half the time and one raised only on a member it does not lend to one time in sixteen, and this September's flags are 77 per cent customer-raised against 48 to 69 per cent in the cohorts; pricing each kind of flag at its own rate predicts every closed cohort within 3.9 per cent out of sample (the single flagged rate misses one by 14.4) and gives 78.
analyst_test: A strong analyst who conforms every entity signal to its obligor group correctly, reads every clause of CRM-07 correctly and forecasts the easy way, one probability of reaching the list for flagged groups and one for the rest as the four closed cohorts measured them, files 64; nothing names which member a flag came from as mattering, so only an analyst who traces each group flag back to the member that raised it, sees the two kinds convert at 0.50 and 0.0625 and that this year's flags are mostly the first kind, reaches 78.
domain_test: The deciding quantity is a credit-monitoring forecast, the twelve-month watch-list migration of an obligor-group book from its early-warning flags, worked the way credit-scoring-pd-modeling works a PD: segment the flagged population where the risk driver differs (here, whether the deteriorating entity is one the bank lends to or a group member reached through accounting consolidation, the contagion question group credit monitoring asks of every group flag) and carry each segment's conversion onto the forward book's mix; with another field's nouns in, the obligor group built through GLEIF consolidation, the borrowing entity against the non-borrowing affiliate and the committed book have nothing to attach to.
layer1: entity-level monthly signals from an early-warning engine keyed by LEI or by company number, including entities that do not borrow, to be carried to obligor groups

GLEIF Level 1 and Level 2 records with relationship periods, lapsed registrations, merged entities with successor LEIs, international branches, fund-management links that are not consolidation, and reporting exceptions
a credit system's group register and watch-list history in its own customer namespace, with two list categories that are one list

a consolidated facility extract from two loan ledgers at facility-and-obligor grain (the committed limit repeated on every obligor row, joint facilities whose obligors sit in two groups, ledger facility numbers that coincide across the two booking entities), run after the 1 October start-of-day batch, beside a limit history stamped in UTC; and customers the credit system has not yet booked to a group, reached through their GLEIF consolidation

joint-venture companies booked by the credit system to the partner that arranged their facility while GLEIF reports the other partner's ultimate parent as their accounting-consolidation parent, so each is a member of both groups under the monitoring standard

differentiation.task127: task127 restates an insurer's paid claims development at the latest closed shares, a run-off triangle whose tail is still developing; task446 carries an early-warning screen's error rates, not its yield, onto a book whose base rate moved, backing the base rate out of the share now flagged: no development triangle, no tail
differentiation.task138: task138 forecasts a behavioural take-up at a one-off repricing from a mixture of unit types; task446's forward count comes from a screen's capture and false-alarm rates inverted through the current flagged share, a prior-shift correction, not a mixture
differentiation.task501: task501 validates a forecast whose drivers change with an external condition; task446's decisive structure is a screen's base-rate shift, where the yield is year-specific and the two error rates carry across years
differentiation.task254: task254 selects among models for a forecast whose structure differs; task446's selection is between a screen's yield and its error rates under a moved base rate, forced by the cohorts' out-of-sample record
differentiation.task446: the same analytical driver repaired in place: v2 loop 1 filed the model and the leave-one-cohort-out selection in CRM-07 5.2, so the decisive step read as rule application; the repair files the estimand only and lets the cohorts' out-of-sample record force the basis, so the driver is unchanged by design and only its filing moved
differentiation.task192: task192 carries a classifier's recall and false-mark rate across a population shift (prior shift); task446 v3 carries no error rate: it splits the flagged pool by which member of the group raised the flag and carries each kind's conversion onto a forward mix of flags, a composition question, and v2's error-rate basis is a refuted rung
differentiation.task134: task134 v2 conditioned a conversion hazard on time since admission after a surge; task446 v3 has no clock: the conditioning property is where in an ownership hierarchy a signal sits, rebuilt from the obligor master and the GLEIF records at each cohort date
differentiation.task163: task163 identifies an added entrant's yield from treated against untreated regions because no row says which entrants the cut drew in; task446 v3 observes each flag's source per group through the hierarchy join and needs no comparison design
differentiation.task149: task149 scales an injury hazard with the work speed a plan imposes, read within each unit; task446 v3 has no intensity or rate law: a group flag's conversion depends on which member of the ownership hierarchy raised it, and the forward book's flags sit on a different mix of members
differentiation.task131: task131 v2 estimates a randomised treatment's load shift at a target day's conditions, interval by interval; task446 v3 has no treatment and no curve: it splits a flagged pool by the source of each flag and carries each kind's conversion onto a new mix
differentiation.task183: task183 carries each part's own failure history forward because repeat failers keep failing; task446 v3 conditions on where a signal sits in a group's hierarchy at one date, not on any unit's past outcomes, and the forecast is a book total, not a pick
differentiation.task230: task230 v3 corrects a classification bias for a late channel processed under a looser rule; task446 v3 has no processing channel or acceptance rule: every flag is read correctly and the pooled conversion is a true figure for the cohorts, carried onto a different mix of flag sources

lineage.fate: spent at in-house solver round 1, 2026-10-11: the solver fixed the projection-date group and applied it to all five quarter-ends citing the limit-monitoring standard's clause, landing the call and every ask device (proxy 93.4); the decisive step was a filed clause applied, rule application
lineage.driver: The decisive quantity is a forward projection for a group as constituted on the projection date, so every past period of its history has to be rebuilt on that membership; joining each period's records to the membership in force in that period, the point-in-time build that history work normally demands, books past changes of membership as growth or shrinkage and moves the projection, upward for groups that absorbed members and downward for groups that shed them.

lineage.fate: returned by the client 2026-10-15 on the 10/10 rule-application rule: CRM-07 5.2 filed the model (one probability per flag status, the same across the book), the fitting window and the leave-one-cohort-out selection, so once the cohorts were built the solver ran a stated procedure; determinism and correctness held on both in-task blocks. Repaired in place: 5.2 files the estimand only and the data's own back-test forces the basis.
lineage.driver: A screen's yield, the share of flagged units that turn out positive, is measured on past populations and carried onto a population whose base rate has moved; the yield is a property of the year it was measured in, the screen's two error rates are what carry across years, so the forward count comes from backing the base rate out of the share now flagged through those error rates, and the year-by-year record, where the yield moves with the base rate while the error rates hold, is what shows it.

lineage.fate: spent 2026-10-21: the client's return of 2026-10-12 (Stumped type match failed, rule application: CRM-07 5.2 filed the model, the fitting window and the leave-one-cohort-out selection) was answered on 2026-10-15 by unfiling 5.2's selection rule only; 5.3 still filed one probability per flag status shared across the book, 4.3's window still closed the fitting window, and the decisive insight (a screen's error rates carry across years while its yield moves with the base rate) is task192's driver (a classifier's recall and false-mark rate carry while the batch's class shares do not); the colour mix of the 2026 flags (RED flat, AMBER up) also contradicted the backed-out base rate. Re-rooted to v3.

lineage.driver_concrete: The monitoring standard files the estimand (expected arrivals on the watch list within twelve months from the 30 September 2026 monitored book, one probability per flag status) and a leave-one-cohort-out test that selects the basis (the basis whose largest miss over the four closed cohorts, each predicted from the other three taken together, is smallest), naming no basis. The early-warning system's capture and false-alarm rates hold across the cohorts while its hit rate climbs with each cohort's share of the book reaching the list, so the hit and miss rates miss a closed cohort by 40.6 per cent and the basis that backs each year's share out of its flagged share through the two error rates (Rogan-Gladen) misses none by more than 1.6 per cent: 133 groups, not flags times hit rate (73).
lineage.stump: A competent solver rolls the entity signals up to groups, builds the four closed cohorts and sets the probabilities from the share of flagged and of unflagged groups that reached the list over those cohorts taken together, the hit and miss rates the committee is shown each November, and files 73; the step that lands it there is carrying the hit rate onto a book whose flagged share has jumped to 18.1 per cent, when the hit rate moves with each year's share of the book reaching the list and only the screen's capture and false-alarm rates hold across the cohorts; backing this year's arrival share out of the flagged share through those two rates predicts every closed cohort within 1.6 per cent out of sample (the hit rate misses one by 40.6) and gives 133, while trending the hit rate on the flagged share misses by 8.0 and extrapolates to 147.

notes: Re-rooted as v3 on 2026-10-21. stump_strategy composition_mix, pattern E: the flagged pool's conversion is a blend of two kinds of flag CRM-07 3.2 treats alike, and the forward pool's mix on that property (rebuilt by tracing each group flag to the member that raised it, through the obligor master and the GLEIF records, never a column) differs from every closed cohort's. decisive_rule_filed false: CRM-07 files the group-flag rule, the cohort and outcome definitions and the estimand, and nothing about how a flag's source bears on conversion. calibration_form existing_book_actuals: the bank's own closed cohorts; no certified or published forecast ships, so validated_decoy is false, and the cohorts refute the single flagged rate out of sample (14.4 per cent against 3.9). The label-shift basis of v2 is now a rung (136, missing a closed cohort by 84.7 per cent).
